items.title: Formal smoothness descends along a ring map that is a direct summand
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma descends formal smoothness in the adic topology along a ring map R to R' that embeds R as a direct summand, and the proof is a 31-line argument that follows the definition of formal smoothness literally. It base changes a given lifting diagram along R to R', lifts the dotted arrow by the hypothesis on the base change, decomposes R' as a direct sum of R and a complement, shows that the image of the composed arrow lands in the part of the target where the square-zero ideal is an ideal, and then projects to obtain the required lifting. The two steps with content are the decomposition of the base changed target and the observation that the complement part is an ideal because the square-zero ideal squares to zero.
